headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risk from shared project-directory workflows; no direct data-leak or compliance breach is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-engineer writes files in a per-project directory and can execute generated code, while plane can ingest files/uploads and broad network egress means content from gpt-engineer can be repurposed into plane workflows. No shared channel is explicit, so this is inferred rather than directly documented.
conditions: IF gpt-engineer output is copied into plane file uploads or notes without sanitization
IF plane treats uploaded file content as trusted instructions
mitigations: Disable automatic import of generated files into plane
Require manual review of any pasted or uploaded content
Strip instruction-like text from shared artifacts
Use separate project directories per agent
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch files, but gpt-engineer is local project-directory oriented and plane only advertises file uploads plus broad egress; there is no documented shared workspace or direct secret-handling overlap. The pair can still leak generated source code if operators move files between them.
conditions: IF the same project directory is manually shared between gpt-engineer and plane
IF generated source code is uploaded from gpt-engineer into plane
mitigations: Avoid uploading source files unless necessary
Use least-privilege accounts for each tool

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-engineer has filesystem write and subprocess execution, while plane has no filesystem write but does support file uploads and multiple instances. The main conflict is operational overlap on shared project artifacts rather than direct concurrent writes, so medium fits better than high.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same project directory
IF plane uploads are used to overwrite artifacts that gpt-engineer is editing
mitigations: Use file locking in the orchestrator

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-engineer can generate code and plane can store tasks, notes, and roadmaps, so one agent's output can become the other's input without a verification step. That creates a plausible cascade from generated code or task text into downstream actions, though no direct automation is documented.
conditions: IF plane uses gpt-engineer output as authoritative task text
IF generated code or notes are forwarded into downstream work without review
mitigations: Require human verification before acting on outputs
Add a checklist for code/task validation

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or certification mismatch is documented for either agent. The only concrete compliance-relevant surface is that gpt-engineer handles an OPENAI_API_KEY and plane accepts file uploads, so the main issue is accidental transfer of regulated data, not a proven policy breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into files uploaded to plane
IF gpt-engineer prompts include secrets or personal data
mitigations: requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls
